title: {{send_tool}} — input
description: Input schema for the SOX send operation (tool name varies by adapter; use {{send_tool}} placeholder in discipline text). Non-blocking: the tool returns as soon as the backing store durably accepts the message. Normative reference: CONTRACTS.md §5.1 and spec/primitives/channels.md.

channel.description: Name of the target channel. Recommended naming conventions: 'ticket:<id>' for task-scoped channels, 'broadcast:<topic>' for one-to-many announcements, 'agent:<id>' for direct messages, 'group:<name>' for named groups, 'thread:<parent-message-id>' for reply threads.

body.description: Opaque message payload. MUST be a JSON object. SOX does not inspect or validate the body beyond requiring it to be an object. Recommended advisory fields: 'type' (string), 'subject' (string), 'context' (string), 'question' (string), 'answer' (string), 'urgency' (one of low/normal/high). Reserved body types with normative schemas: 'sox-ack' (spec/envelopes/sox-ack.schema.json), 'sox-nack' (spec/envelopes/sox-nack.schema.json), 'sox-error' is not sent by agents, 'sox-invite' (spec/envelopes/sox-invite.schema.json).

correlation_id.description: Optional caller-supplied correlation token. Stored verbatim and echoed back in recv output. Use for: request-reply pairing, at-least-once deduplication, thread anchoring. The protocol does not enforce uniqueness. Null when not needed.

body.subject: Which schema version to target?
body.context: Implementing the auth migration. The task spec mentions v2 but production shows v3.
body.question: Should I target schema v2 or v3?
